desc: Ask [C2]: Summarize my Java study notes.

{"id":5,"answer":"Here's a summary of the Java-related notes I have for you. Each bullet is tagged with the note it comes from.

Collections
- ArrayList vs LinkedList (note 3): ArrayList is array-backed, so get(i) is O(1) random access; LinkedList is O(n) for get(i) but O(1) insert/remove at the ends. You flagged that you keep mixing these two up for your DSA exam.
  `list.get(0);   // ArrayList: O(1)   LinkedList: O(n)`
  `deque.addFirst(x); // LinkedList: O(1)`
- HashMap vs Hashtable (note 23): HashMap allows one null key and multiple null values; Hashtable allows neither. HashMap is not synchronized.
  `map.put(null, "v"); // HashMap: OK   Hashtable: NullPointerException`

Exceptions
- Checked vs unchecked (note 28): checked exceptions must be declared or caught; unchecked ones are RuntimeException subclasses. try-with-resources closes resources in reverse order of declaration.
  `try (var a = open(); var b = open()) { ... } // b closes before a`

Generics
- Type erasure (note 4): `List<String>` becomes plain `List` at runtime, so `instanceof List<String>` is illegal and `new T[]` isn't allowed. This is also why generic varargs produce unchecked warnings.
  `if (x instanceof List<String>) { } // compile error — use List<?>`

Framework gotchas
- Spring @Transactional (note 17): it only works through the proxy, so self-invocation bypasses it — the same trap as @Cacheable.
  `this.save(); // self-call: goes around the proxy, no transaction applied`

OOP principles
- Inheritance and LSP (note 5): your professor's point that inheritance is for substitutability, not code reuse — if B is-a A, anywhere A works, B must work. You noted you want to re-read the LSP chapter.

Scope note: this covers only the Java items in your notes. Other notes in the same set are not Java material (e.g. Python default-argument evaluation, SQLite FTS5, system-design interview prep, and DeepNotes product feedback), so I left them out.
